259 |     The request is authenticated using Django's object-level permissions.

262 |     It ensures that the user is authenticated, and has the appropriate
263 |     `add`/`change`/`delete` permissions on the object using .has_perms.
264 | 
265 |     This permission can only be applied against view classes that
266 |     provide a `.queryset` attribute.
267 |     """
268 |     perms_map = {
269 |         'GET': [],
270 |         'OPTIONS': [],
271 |         'HEAD': [],
272 |         'POST': ['%(app_label)s.add_%(model_name)s'],
273 |         'PUT': ['%(app_label)s.change_%(model_name)s'],
274 |         'PATCH': ['%(app_label)s.change_%(model_name)s'],
275 |         'DELETE': ['%(app_label)s.delete_%(model_name)s'],
276 |     }
277 | 
278 |     def get_required_object_permissions(self, method, model_cls):
279 |         kwargs = {
280 |             'app_label': model_cls._meta.app_label,
281 |             'model_name': model_cls._meta.model_name
282 |         }
283 | 
284 |         if method not in self.perms_map:
285 |             raise exceptions.MethodNotAllowed(method)
286 | 
287 |         return [perm % kwargs for perm in self.perms_map[method]]

290 |         # authentication checks have already executed via has_permission
291 |         queryset = self._queryset(view)
292 |         model_cls = queryset.model
293 |         user = request.user

295 |         perms = self.get_required_object_permissions(request.method, model_cls)
296 | 
297 |         if not user.has_perms(perms, obj):
298 |             # If the user does not have permissions we need to determine if
299 |             # they have read permissions to see 403, or not, and simply see
300 |             # a 404 response.

302 |             if request.method in SAFE_METHODS:
